issue: In tqdm.contrib.tenumerate, the start argument must set the first index returned by enumeration. For a two-item iterable and start=5, the indexes must be 5 and 6. Keep the default start at 0 and preserve the existing function signature. Run the tests.

When a custom bar containing ANSI control codes is shortened to ncols, do not append a second reset sequence if the trimmed result already ends with an ANSI reset. Keep the visible width correct and run the tests.

A tqdm instance wrapping an iterable without a known length must have a defined truth value. Casting it to bool should be true without consuming the iterable. Preserve the behavior for known totals and run the tests.

tqdm.format_meter must support numeric unit_scale when total is unknown (None). Scale the completed count and rate without trying to multiply an unknown total; keep known-total formatting working. Run the tests.
A disabled tqdm instance with an explicit total must retain that total so its truth value is defined: total=10 is true and total=0 is false. Keep disabled progress display behavior and run the tests.

Wrapping an iterator with no known length in a disabled tqdm instance must still allow consumers such as list() to iterate successfully. Do not require a total attribute that may not exist on the disabled instance. Run the tests.

The tqdm CLI option parser must recognize --name only at the beginning of input or after whitespace. A double dash inside ordinary text such as value--oops is not a new option. Preserve normal --total parsing and run the tests.

tqdm.format_meter must honor a user bar_format that contains {bar}. Format the user-supplied left and right segments around the progress bar, including placeholders such as {n_fmt} and {total_fmt}. Run the tests.

format_sizeof must choose SI units based on the value that will be displayed after rounding. Values near 10, 100, and 1000 should not render as misleading 10.00, 100.0, or 1000 in the smaller unit. Run the tests.
